lead: there is an answer ready for what you will be doing now, and it has been ready for years, and none of it is true. five people have taken it at a doorway and gone in satisfied.
sun: the question comes at the same place every time. somebody about to walk in alone turns at the last moment, decent about it, and asks what you will do now — and the boundary is the one point where there is nothing to report. every hour of the months before it had a next thing in it. the hour on the other side has none, and that is the hour they ask about.
moon: the covering goes over the interval instead — the drive home, the fortnight after, the season with nobody in it to take anywhere. no held story sits under there and never has, which is the reason for the covering: an absence cannot be shown to anybody. the whole arrangement stands on one point of contact, and that point is somebody currently needing a route.
pull: nothing under the cover was ever worth concealing. what holds it up is the next person needing a route, and there has always been a next person.
tension: the account people settle on is that you are private, and it arrives as a compliment, generally from someone you gave months of close attention. it is the wrong shape. a private person has an interior being withheld, and the offer that keeps coming — tell me about your own year, for once — assumes there is a year to tell. saying otherwise is the worst sentence available about a life, so the compliment stands and the offer keeps arriving.
cost: whole years of somebody's worst months pass with nothing of yours in them — no bad week to work around, no state to read on arrival — which is most of why people can be taken anywhere by you. no part of the covering comes down gradually. the season with nobody to walk is the season it stands on nothing, and none of the five would know what is left.

lead: you have lived on the same street since you were twenty-four, and nine people have been taken out of it by you, the whole way, and not one of those trips lasted longer than a week.
sun: the hospital in another city, the hearing, the flat that has to be seen by friday — each of those takes days out of your life and no more. you know the turning people miss, you take them past it and stop at the door. each is invisible from where you live, because the only evidence it happened is a person who is no longer on the street.
moon: what you set up has an inside. twenty-six years of it: who holds whose key, which door gets knocked when the heating fails, what happens the week somebody dies. nobody living in it has ever had occasion to name it, since it has not once failed, and a thing that does not fail generates none. it is the one thing here that will still be standing after you.
pull: nine people were taken to the edge of a life by you. none of it shows from here, because every trip was short and the street has never once looked up to find you missing.
tension: somebody who moved in recently will say it warmly, at a door, holding a parcel: that you will be here when the rest of them have gone. the observation is sound. you have never left. what it has no room for is the nine times you went out ahead of a person to the edge of something enormous and turned round, each of which took three days and left a gap nobody standing here was ever going to notice.
cost: at four hours' notice a person in trouble gets all of it, and nothing at the far end is wanted from them, because your own end was never in question — the street holds on wednesday whether or not you are on it. the journey that has never come up is the one that ends somewhere you would have to stay. nothing here has ever needed you to find out.

lead: no part of this life is going anywhere on its own account. the work, the money, the evenings, each of them is a delivery, and there is nothing opposite that to pull the other way.
sun: rooms sort into travellers around you inside an evening. the stuck one says so; the ones who are not stuck talk to each other; and this has happened everywhere you have ever been, including at your own table. nobody has to be told what you are for. no relationship here has ever needed starting, and there has never been one running on anything else.
moon: a situation resolves into a route before the person has finished describing it. three sentences about a bad year and the way out is laid out in order with the difficult part marked, at dinner, in a queue, on holiday, with nobody having asked. there is no other setting to put the instrument in. a week with nobody to take anywhere leaves the whole of it running against nothing.
pull: every road you have ever learned was learned for somebody else's arrival. doubled, with no second register in you, there is not one in the whole set that leads home.
tension: it gets tried the other way. somebody who loves you tries to do for you what you did for four of theirs — the introduction, the flat, the job three hundred miles off — and gets a month in before it stops, having found no far side to walk you to. the reading they leave with is that you would not be helped. what gave out is that a person can only be taken where they were already going.
cost: forty people are living where they were trying to get to, and the difficult ones got the length the easy ones got, because nothing in you argues for stopping and no other appetite is bidding for the week. what the record holds is far sides. not one of the addresses in it is a place you have stood, and no second half of you was ever built to collect one.

lead: she sat the last one at forty-six and cannot name a point anywhere in the six years before it where something started or something stopped. terms and exams gave it edges from outside. it had none.
sun: the going does not come in stages. everyone else works in referrals: a hand-off to whoever does the next part, and every seam in that arrangement is a place where somebody quietly stops. what you run has no seam anywhere: the first evening at her kitchen table and the drive to the last exam are one continuous piece at one pull, and nothing in the middle was ever set down and taken up again.
moon: the pull came from her end too, for six years, which is the part nobody credits her with — a length does no work unless both ends haul. what that makes is one motion rather than a series of acts — not describable in pieces, not available for anybody else to take up halfway. and it comes off the way a line comes off, all at once, at the door.
pull: six years at one tension and no knot anywhere in it. she got there, you let go at the door, and neither of you could point at a single thing that happened.
tension: three of them have described the months after as worse than the years before, and each put it down to their own character — an anticlimax, an ingratitude they were ashamed of. what came off at the door was a pull they had stopped registering years earlier, and it came off whole. saying so turns a finished delivery into something done to a person, so her account is what stands, and in it the trouble was hers.
cost: nothing gets lost in a handover, since none happens — the fourth year runs at the tension of the first fortnight, and people everybody else has given up on feel that inside a month. the length is set at the other end. six years of yours was decided by how far she had to go, and on the morning she arrived the whole of it came off at once.
